mechanical-whale.teaser: A printed mechanism, a tested joint, and the next round of correction.

items.alt: White skeletal whale prototype with a crank and wave-shaped supports, presented against a retouched charcoal background
items.caption: Presentation edit from Brian’s assembly photograph. The background was cleaned with AI; use the original photos below for the physical development record.

items.alt: White mechanical whale assembled on a tabletop beside its empty kit frame and loose washers
items.caption: The supplied assembly photo shows a real printed iteration. It does not establish that the complete powered mechanism has passed testing.

items.alt: White printed hinge and collar test piece on a dark desk
items.caption: Brian reported that this hinge and collar printed well and moved successfully. That result applies to this component, not the full assembly.

easter-tomb.teaser: The real printed assembly makes the next design problem visible.

items.alt: Close view of the printed Easter Tomb cross-shaft and cord drums against a cleaned dark background
items.caption: Background-retouched presentation of the partially assembled mechanism. The cord drums were under revision; the image is not evidence of a completed working model.

items.alt: Cream-colored printed cord drums and supports in the partially assembled Easter Tomb model
items.caption: An original development photo records the drum and cord-routing problem. The later replacement drums still needed a physical test.

cedar-bracket-cover-planters.teaser: Measured constraints become physical cedar covers and planters.

items.alt: Three unfinished cedar covers and planters grouped around a timber, with a retouched dark background
items.caption: AI-retouched presentation based on Brian’s supplied build photo. Customer delivery is owner-reported; the photograph does not establish a load rating.

items.alt: Close view of unfinished cedar trim, rough grain and a visible screw at a planter corner
items.caption: Original close-up of the cedar build. Material texture and the visible fastener remain as photographed.

scribr.teaser: A working local transcription application, shown with an empty input.

items.alt: Scribr’s dark transcription interface with an empty source field and local processing status
items.caption: Saved application capture from July 2026. This empty-state view contains no customer transcript or job history. Public availability remains separate from local operation.

wing-light.teaser: A native game pilot with a quiet visual language and one-touch play.

items.alt: Wing and Light calm-mode screen with a glowing bird, cloud tunnel and tap-anywhere instruction
items.caption: Saved simulator capture of the calm-mode interface. Brian reports physical-device testing separately; this screenshot itself is simulator evidence.

items.alt: Wing and Light home screen with Play, Daily Trial, Cosmetics, Missions, Achievements and Settings controls
items.caption: Saved home-screen capture from the pilot. The screen documents the interface, not a public App Store release.

living-lights.teaser: Visible light, wiring, and hardware from the outdoor prototype.

items.alt: Warm Living Lights prototype nodes glowing among plants and branches at night
items.caption: Existing outdoor prototype photo. The project record includes hardware development and field-observation limits.

items.alt: Living Lights ESP32 development board mounted in a blue terminal carrier
items.caption: Existing project hardware photo; active prototype.

arc-forge.teaser: Visual development for a systems-engineering game.

items.alt: ARC FORGE machinery with cyan, purple and orange energy systems
items.caption: Existing public visual-development asset. Artwork does not establish gameplay completion or release.
